from_session: Four levers tested and four killed on evidence; H3 shipped a conditional 5-step stage 1, a 4K tier and its docs; the board went from 19 cards in doing to 5

session.name: H3 performance hunt that produced four negatives, plus a board and rules clean-up

goal.original: Continue handoff 651ea97d (MPI-476's re-check), then follow the user's live H3 testing wherever it led.
goal.summary: MPI-476 closed. The evening became a hunt for why H3 feels slow on a 4060 Ti, and its main output is FOUR DEAD ENDS, each killed with evidence so none can be re-run: the --lowvram flag, the beta scheduler, moving the sigma split alone, and (from the prior session) the latent hi-res fix. What shipped instead: ref2va now samples stage 1 at 5 steps when a reference image is present, a 4K tier, a trimmed tooltip, and a large docs pass. Separately the board was swept 19 -> 5 and the rule that let it rot is now written down.

completed: --lowvram IS INERT AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. ComfyUI 0.30.0 + torch 2.13 + comfy_aimdo 0.4.11 means dynamic VRAM is on, and model_management.py L983 puts LOW_VRAM and NORMAL_VRAM in the SAME branch on the SAME budget - no vram_state branch anywhere distinguishes them. The user ran it flagless anyway (correctly): 7m05s against --lowvram baselines of 7m12/7m22/7m23. routes/comfy.js was patched for the test and REVERTED.

beta vs simple: NO speed difference and simple SHIPS, decided on AUDIO. simple reproduced 167s twice; beta gave 141s and 196s - a 55s spread on itself against the 26s 'win' the first pair appeared to show. beta is slightly better on some textures but markedly worse on sound. Established the rule that generalises: H3 emits video and audio from ONE joint latent, so every sampler/scheduler/step/split change must be LISTENED to, not just looked at.

THE SIGMA SPLIT REALLOCATES, IT DOES NOT SHORTEN. Both SamplerCustomAdvanced nodes share a guider, a model and a latent size with no upscale between them, so 5/15 and 10/10 are both 20 steps and the same wall clock. What a smaller split DOES buy free is a 2x faster PREVIEW (progressStages preview: 1 = stage 1 alone).

SHIPPED: ref2va samples stage 1 at 5 steps when a reference image is present (6cd5857e). MpiLoadImageFromPath's height output is 0 on an empty path, so it is the presence flag with no extra injected node: Input_Image.height -> MpiCompare '== 0' -> MpiMath '10 if a else 5' -> SplitSigmas.step. Measured: 5 steps holds with a reference and collapses to mush without one. Audio-clean too - every run in the beta/simple comparison already used a 5-step stage 1.

SHIPPED: a 4K tier on H3 (0f1ed1ca), LTX's numbers, /32-clean, asserted across all seven tiers, and marked in-comment as the one tier with no run behind it. The ladder deliberately stops at ONE entry per high-res class rather than a second full quality ladder at 2K - that shape question is settled, do not reopen. npm test 492/492.
SHIPPED: the Reference detail tooltip was 249 chars against a 57-108 house norm and the status bar truncated it mid-sentence; trimmed to 107, dropped half moved into ref2va.md.

MEASURED: max vs match is ~1.7x (12 min vs 7 min) for a real quality gain, from reference resolution ALONE with the output canvas identical. That settles the standing question of whether reference tokens dominate per-step cost. They do. Also: max caps the reference at a 2048px edge, so a 2688px character sheet is downscaled, not passed whole.

BOARD SWEPT 19 -> 5, and the rule that let it rot is now in .claude/rules/kanban.md and .claude/skills/mpi-end/SKILL.md: validating is not a parking space. Agent evidence is sufficient to close; work needing a human judgement gets ASKED in-session; a silent park is the defect.

TWO SILENT-ACCUMULATION DEFECTS FIXED: the global .agents/mpi-kanban/events.jsonl had stopped at the previous session (15 events backfilled - _schema.md requires BOTH the card log and the global one), and state/index.json claimed 10 active handoffs of which 8 were resolved or superseded (swept to 2).

key_decisions: FOUR DEAD ENDS, DO NOT RE-RUN ANY OF THEM: (1) --lowvram is inert under aimdo - proven in source AND measured at 7m05 vs 7m12/7m22/7m23; (2) beta vs simple - no reproducible speed difference and beta loses on AUDIO; (3) moving the sigma split alone saves nothing because both stages cost the same per step; (4) the latent hi-res fix, killed the previous session by elimination. Each has its evidence written where the next reader will hit it.

The remaining untested speed lever is BasicScheduler.steps 20 -> 15 with the split at 5 (= 5 + 10, ~25%). It is a trajectory change of exactly the kind that just cost beta the comparison, so it MUST be judged on audio, not picture. A second MpiMath off the existing node 379 boolean is all the wiring it needs.

Also untested: --reserve-vram. class MiniMaxH3 declares neither memory_usage_factor_conds nor extra_conds_shapes, while Flux2, Qwen and every Wan variant do - so H3's weight budget is computed from the output latent alone and the references count as zero. That is source-verified fact; the causal link to the slowdown is NOT measured. See MPI-478.

H3 is 53GB of weights on a 16GB card and footprint.js says that wants ~40GB of RAM. Slowness there is largely the machine, not a bug - the product's own answer is the remote engine. Do not chase VRAM readings: residency is set by what is LEFT OVER after the latent estimate, so a SMALLER canvas shows MORE weights resident (14.5GB at 960x544 vs 13.7GB on bigger runs). Measure s/it, never the VRAM number.

Time per-step changes at the medium tier or above, NEVER at a 1-second clip. Fixed overhead that is 2.5% of a 7-minute run is 8-18% of a 141s one, and that is exactly how the phantom beta 'win' appeared.
